title: How Congress Should Tackle Corruption
gist: FP Live event page (Nov. 23, 2026) previewing Casey Michel's roadmap for the new Democratic Congress to tackle corruption: investigations into Trump family businesses, illicit pardons and foreign influence-buying, followed by campaign finance and money-laundering reform and possibly a constitutional amendment. Thin promotional page; also notes midterm voters were driven by tariffs and Iran-war gas prices.

insights.claim: Polls show Americans were angry about government corruption when voting in the midterms, giving Democrats a perceived mandate to act on it.
insights.speaker: Dana Sherne
insights.so_what: Expect corruption oversight to dominate the new Congress's agenda.
insights.quote: Numerous polls show that Americans were angry about government corruption

insights.claim: Casey Michel proposes Democrats start with investigations into Trump family businesses, illicit pardons and foreign entities' attempts to buy White House influence.
insights.speaker: Dana Sherne
insights.so_what: Trump-linked business ventures face subpoena and headline risk.
insights.quote: start with investigations into the Trump family businesses, illicit pardons, and attempts by foreign entities to buy influence in the White House

insights.claim: After investigations, Michel's roadmap calls for sweeping campaign finance and money-laundering reforms and even a constitutional amendment.
insights.speaker: Dana Sherne
insights.so_what: Longer-dated AML/campaign-finance reform could raise compliance burdens for financial intermediaries.

insights.claim: Democrats retook both chambers in the Nov. 3 midterms, with foreign policy an unusually strong driver because tariffs raised everyday prices and the Iran war sent gas prices soaring.
insights.speaker: Dana Sherne
insights.so_what: Tariffs and war-driven fuel costs are now politically constrained in Trump's final two years.
insights.quote: Tariffs have raised the price of everyday goods, and the war with Iran has sent gas prices soaring.
insights.locator: What the Midterms Mean for U.S. Foreign Policy

insights.claim: Trump's so-called energy cease-fire has not stopped Russian strikes on Ukrainian power and oil infrastructure or Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries, even as the U.S. begins buying Russian diesel.
insights.speaker: Dana Sherne
insights.so_what: Refinery attacks keep diesel markets tight; U.S. purchases of Russian diesel signal product shortage.
insights.quote: even as the United States begins to purchase Russian diesel
